The proposed answer 3^2025 is correct.

**Adjacency check.** Let M = 2^n − 1. Layer n+1 then has 2^(n+1) − 1 = 2M+1 bricks. Brick k in layer n spans [(k−1)/M, k/M], and brick j in layer n+1 spans [(j−1)/(2M+1), j/(2M+1)]. They share a side exactly when their intervals overlap in positive length, which means:

- (k−1)/M < j/(2M+1), so j > 2k−2 + (k−1)/M, which gives j ≥ 2k−1.
- (j−1)/(2M+1) < k/M, so j < 2k+1 + k/M, which gives j ≤ 2k+1. This holds even at k = M, since 2M+1 = 2k+1 is the last brick.

I also checked the neighbouring candidates directly. Brick 2k−2 fails because (k−1)(2M+1) < (2k−2)M would need k < 1. Brick 2k+2 fails because it would need M < k. So every brick k has exactly the three neighbours 2k−1, 2k, 2k+1 below it.

**Boundary check.** If 1 ≤ k ≤ 2^i − 1, then 2k−1 ≥ 1 and 2k+1 ≤ 2^(i+1) − 1. All three choices therefore always exist.

**Count.** Jessica makes 2025 moves, each with 3 choices, and different choice sequences give different brick sequences. The total is 3^2025.

**Numerical check.** log10(3^2025) ≈ 966.1705, so 3^2025 has 967 digits and leading digits near 10^0.1705 ≈ 1.481. This matches the printed number, which begins 1480951….
